title: Boundary Stones of the District of Columbia
artist: Surveyed by Andrew Ellicott and Benjamin Banneker
location: Around the edge of the original 10-mile square; e.g. the East Cornerstone at Southern Ave & Eastern Ave
description: Forty stones set a mile apart to mark the original diamond-shaped District, surveyed by Andrew Ellicott with the help of Benjamin Banneker. About 36 survive, making them the oldest federal monuments in the country.

title: Washington Monument
location: 2 15th St NW, National Mall
description: The 555-foot marble obelisk honoring George Washington. Begun in 1848, it stood half-finished for over 20 years during and after the Civil War; look for the change in marble color about a third of the way up. Completed in 1884 and dedicated in 1885.

title: Andrew Jackson
location: Center of Lafayette Square, across from the White House
description: Jackson raises his hat while his horse rears on its hind legs. It was the first bronze statue cast in the United States and the first equestrian statue balanced on only two legs.

title: George Washington
location: Washington Circle NW
description: Washington on horseback at the Battle of Princeton, set in one of the traffic circles from Pierre L'Enfant's original city plan, at the edge of George Washington University.

title: Statue of Freedom
location: Top of the U.S. Capitol dome
description: The bronze woman crowning the Capitol dome, wearing a helmet topped with an eagle's head and feathers. Philip Reid, an enslaved craftsman at the foundry, worked out how to separate the plaster model so it could be cast. She was raised into place in December 1863.

title: Abraham Lincoln (City Hall)
location: In front of the old D.C. City Hall, 451 Indiana Ave NW
description: A standing marble Lincoln paid for by Washington residents and unveiled on the third anniversary of his death. Flannery had been in Ford's Theatre the night Lincoln was shot. It is the oldest surviving public memorial to Lincoln in the country.

title: Winfield Scott
location: Scott Circle NW
description: The long-serving general who led U.S. forces in the Mexican-American War, cast from cannons captured in that war.

title: John A. Rawlins
location: Rawlins Park, 18th St & E St NW
description: Standing bronze of Ulysses S. Grant's chief of staff and later Secretary of War, in the small park that bears his name. It was moved around the city more than once before returning to Rawlins Park.

title: Emancipation Memorial (Lincoln & Archer Alexander)
location: West end of Lincoln Park, E Capitol St & 11th St SE
description: Lincoln holds the Emancipation Proclamation over a kneeling freedman modeled on Archer Alexander. Paid for by donations from formerly enslaved people; Frederick Douglass spoke at the dedication. Long debated for its imagery.

title: James B. McPherson
location: Center of McPherson Square, 15th St & K St NW
description: Union general James B. McPherson on horseback, one of the highest-ranking Union officers killed in the war, at the Battle of Atlanta in 1864.

title: Nathanael Greene
location: Center of Stanton Park, Massachusetts Ave & 5th St NE
description: Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene, George Washington's trusted second, on horseback. By the same sculptor as the Winfield Scott statue.

title: Peace Monument
location: Peace Circle, Pennsylvania Ave & 1st St NW
description: Honors Navy sailors and Marines who died in the Civil War. At the top, a weeping figure of Grief buries her face on the shoulder of History, who holds a tablet reading “They died that their country might live.”

title: George H. Thomas
location: Center of Thomas Circle, 14th St & Massachusetts Ave NW
description: Union general George H. Thomas, the “Rock of Chickamauga,” on horseback. Thomas was a Virginian who stayed loyal to the Union.

title: David G. Farragut
location: Center of Farragut Square NW
description: The Navy's first admiral, cast from the propeller of his flagship USS Hartford. Ream was the first woman to receive a federal commission for a statue.

title: Joseph Henry
location: In front of the Smithsonian Castle, 1000 Jefferson Dr SW
description: Physicist Joseph Henry, a pioneer of electromagnetism and the first Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, stands outside the Castle where he lived and worked.

title: Martin Luther
artist: Cast from Ernst Rietschel's statue in Worms, Germany
location: Luther Place Memorial Church, Thomas Circle NW
description: A copy of the Protestant reformer's statue in Worms, Germany, unveiled for the 400th anniversary of Luther's birth outside a Lutheran church built as a memorial to peace after the Civil War.

title: James A. Garfield Monument
location: Garfield Circle, 1st St & Maryland Ave SW
description: President James A. Garfield, assassinated in 1881 after just months in office, stands above three seated figures representing his life as a scholar, soldier, and statesman.

title: Benjamin Franklin
location: Old Post Office, 1100 Pennsylvania Ave NW
description: Standing marble Franklin, a gift to the city from newspaper publisher Stilson Hutchins, in front of the building that served as the city's main post office (Franklin was the first Postmaster General).

title: Adams Memorial (“Grief”)
location: Rock Creek Cemetery, 201 Allison St NW
description: A mysterious shrouded bronze figure seated before a granite wall, commissioned by historian Henry Adams for the grave of his wife, Clover. Often called one of the finest sculptures in America.

title: Marquis de Lafayette
location: Southeast corner of Lafayette Square
description: The young French general who fought beside Washington in the Revolution, shown appealing to the French National Assembly for support of the American cause. The square is named for him.

title: Winfield Scott Hancock
location: Pennsylvania Ave & 7th St NW, U.S. Navy Memorial plaza
description: Union general Winfield Scott Hancock, a hero of Gettysburg, on horseback above Pennsylvania Avenue.

title: Daniel Webster
location: Massachusetts Ave & N St NW, beside Scott Circle
description: The great orator and senator from Massachusetts stands near the site of his former home, above granite reliefs of his famous debates.

title: Samuel Hahnemann
location: East side of Scott Circle NW
description: A seated bronze of the German physician who founded homeopathy, set in a curved granite exedra with relief panels from his life.

title: John A. Logan
location: Center of Logan Circle NW
description: Union general and senator John A. Logan on horseback. Logan helped create Memorial Day in 1868 as head of the Union veterans' organization.

title: Comte de Rochambeau
location: Southwest corner of Lafayette Square
description: The French general who led France's army alongside Washington at Yorktown, pointing the way forward. A gift from France, it was the second of the square's four corner statues.
